title: Economics of inequality and poverty (incl. 2.12 equity)
summary: Markets do not guarantee a fair distribution. Inequality is measured with Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients; poverty can be absolute or relative. Taxes, transfers and public provision redistribute. HL calculates average and marginal tax rates.

keyterms.definition: Equality means everyone has the same; equity means fairness, which may involve unequal treatment.
Differences in income between individuals or households.
Differences in the ownership of assets such as property, shares and savings; usually greater than income inequality.
A curve showing the cumulative % of income received by the cumulative % of households; the further from the diagonal, the more unequal.
A measure of inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality), based on the Lorenz curve.
Income below what is needed for basic needs, e.g. below the World Bank international poverty line (about $3 a day at PPP).
Income below a set share of the median income in a country, e.g. below 50% or 60% of the median.
A measure of poverty across health, education and living standards indicators.
A tax where the average tax rate rises as income rises, taking a larger share from higher incomes.
A tax where the average tax rate falls as income rises, so lower earners pay a larger share of income.
A tax where the average rate stays the same at all incomes (a flat tax).
Payments from government to individuals with no output in return, e.g. pensions and unemployment benefits.
The tax rate paid on an additional unit of income.

questions.statement: Equity and equality mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: Equity is fairness; an equitable distribution may still be unequal.

questions.prompt: On a Lorenz curve diagram, what does the diagonal line represent?
questions.explanation: Along the diagonal, each x% of households receives x% of income.

questions.text: A Gini coefficient closer to 1 indicates more ___.
questions.explanation: 0 is perfect equality; 1 is perfect inequality.

questions.prompt: Country A has a Gini of 0.28, Country B 0.52. Which statement is correct?
options: Income is more unequally distributed in B
A’s Lorenz curve is further from the diagonal
questions.explanation: A higher Gini means a Lorenz curve further from the line of equality. It says nothing directly about poverty or GDP.

questions.prompt: Match each term with its meaning.

pairs.right: Deprivation in health, education, living standards

questions.explanation: Different measures capture different aspects of disadvantage.

questions.statement: Relative poverty can exist even in very rich countries.
questions.explanation: It is defined relative to the country’s median income.

questions.prompt: Which is a cause of rising income inequality?
options: Technological change that raises demand for high-skilled workers
questions.explanation: Skill-biased technology widens wage gaps; the others tend to reduce inequality.

questions.text: Inequality in the ownership of assets is called ___ inequality.
questions.explanation: Wealth generates income (rent, dividends), which can widen income gaps over time.

questions.prompt: Why might markets fail to achieve equity?
options: Incomes reflect factor ownership and bargaining power, not need
questions.explanation: Those who own little capital or have scarce skills earn little in a free market.

questions.prompt: Order the poverty cycle for a low-income household.
items: Little spending on education and health
questions.explanation: Poverty can be self-reinforcing across generations.

options: A sales tax (VAT) on most goods
A tax on luxury cars only
questions.explanation: Poorer households spend a higher share of income, so VAT takes a larger share of their income.

questions.statement: With a progressive tax, higher earners pay a higher average tax rate.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of a progressive tax.

questions.text: A tax with the same average rate at all incomes is a ___ tax.
questions.explanation: Also called a flat tax.
Transfers redistribute income with no output in return.

questions.prompt: Match each policy to how it reduces inequality.

pairs.right: Raises future earnings of the poor

questions.explanation: Redistribution uses taxes, transfers, provision and regulation.

questions.prompt: A possible drawback of very high marginal income tax rates is that they…
options: may reduce incentives to work and invest
questions.explanation: High rates can discourage effort and encourage tax avoidance.

questions.statement: Universal free healthcare can reduce inequality in living standards even if income inequality is unchanged.
questions.explanation: In-kind provision raises the real welfare of low-income households.

questions.prompt: Which policy would most directly reduce wealth inequality?
options: A cut in the top income tax rate
questions.explanation: Taxes on assets target wealth concentration.

questions.text: Payments from government to individuals with no output in return are ___ payments.
questions.explanation: Pensions and benefits are examples.

questions.prompt: Order the redistribution effect of a progressive tax funding cash benefits.
items: Higher earners pay a larger share of income in tax
The Lorenz curve moves closer to the diagonal
questions.explanation: Taxes and transfers together reduce post-tax inequality.

questions.prompt: Tax bands: 0% on the first $10 000; 20% on $10 001–$40 000; 40% above $40 000. How much tax does someone earning $60 000 pay?

questions.text: Same bands: the average tax rate on $60 000 is ___% (1 d.p.).

questions.statement: In the same system, the marginal tax rate for someone earning $60 000 is 40%.
questions.explanation: An extra dollar of income falls in the top band.

questions.prompt: Same bands: tax on an income of $25 000 is…
The average tax rate on $25 000 in this system is…

questions.statement: This tax system is progressive because the average tax rate rises from 12% to 23.3% as income rises.
questions.explanation: Rising average rates with income define a progressive tax.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its calculation.
questions.explanation: In a progressive system, the marginal rate is above the average rate.

questions.prompt: A household earning $20 000 pays $1 000 in sales tax; one earning $80 000 pays $2 000. The sales tax is…
questions.explanation: The richer household pays more dollars but a smaller share of income.

questions.text: A worker’s income rises from $40 000 to $41 000 and her tax rises by $300. Her marginal tax rate is ___%.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to calculate tax in a banded system.
items: Multiply each slice by its band rate
Add the tax from each band
Divide by total income for the average rate
questions.explanation: Only income within each band is taxed at that band’s rate.
